sections.html:
Culpeper County is a Piedmont county in the foothills of the Blue Ridge, about 383 square miles, with the town of Culpeper as its seat. The 2020 census counted 52,552 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 57,666.

Rivers mark two of its edges. The Rappahannock forms the northeast border and the Rapidan the south, while the Hazel River runs east through the middle. Rolling hills slope to the south and east, and the highest point, near the west corner, is 705 feet above sea level.

The county was created in 1749, and its first surveyor was a teenage George Washington. Wikipedia records that the first Culpeper court met that May at the home of Robert Tureman, and Washington was commissioned surveyor in July at age 17.

The name comes from Catherine Culpeper, whose family held the Northern Neck proprietary. In 1833 the upper 267 square miles were split off to form Rappahannock County. Two Civil War engagements took place on Culpeper soil: Cedar Mountain on August 9, 1862, and Brandy Station on June 9, 1863. The Brandy Station Battlefield Park is among the county's protected areas.

The county is also home to Commonwealth Park, site of many equestrian events, and the Culpeper Minutemen, a militia raised here, fought in both the Revolutionary War and the Civil War, per Wikipedia.

sections.h2: What do Culpeper County residents do for work?
sections.html:
Most Culpeper workers leave the county for their jobs. Wikipedia, citing Virginia Employment Commission data, reports a civilian workforce of 24,313, with 30 percent of residents working in the county and 70 percent commuting out, mostly to Fairfax and Fauquier counties.

The largest non-government employers listed as of March 2023 are:

  • Culpeper Memorial Hospital
  • Walmart
  • Masco (Cabinetworks)
  • S.W.I.F.T.
  • Bingham and Taylor Corporation
  • Continental Automotive
  • Cintas Corporation

The same source says in-commuters equal about 45 percent of the local workforce, with the most coming from Orange County.

sections.h2: Which roads and neighbors frame Culpeper County?
sections.html:
US 15, US 29, US 211 and US 522 are the main U.S. routes, joined by state routes 3, 229 and 299.

Six counties border it: Fauquier to the north, Stafford to the east, Spotsylvania to the southeast, Orange to the south, Madison to the southwest and Rappahannock to the northwest. Wikipedia says the Blue Ridge, including Old Rag Mountain and the Skyline Drive, is quickly reached up Route 522.

Outside the town, communities named in the county article include Brandy Station (a census-designated place), Stevensburg, Jeffersonton, Rixeyville, Lignum and Richardsville.

The 2020 census counted 18,181 households, a median age of 39.8 and a 5.2 percent vacancy rate across 19,185 housing units. Culpeper County Public Schools covers the whole county. Wikipedia lists Culpeper County High School and Eastern View High School as its high schools, with the Culpeper Technical Education Center also listed. Culpeper Middle and Floyd T. Binns Middle are the middle schools.

Elementary schools named include A.G. Richardson, Emerald Hill, Farmington, Pearl Sample, Sycamore Park and Yowell. Check the district's current attendance zones for a given address before quoting a school name to a buyer.

sections.h2: What is the Culpeper County real estate tax rate?
sections.html:
The county's real estate tax page lists a 2026 rate of $0.37 for real estate plus $0.08 for fire and rescue, a total of $0.45 per $100 of assessed value. The Town of Culpeper adds $0.061.

At the 2026 total, a house assessed at $400,000 carries $1,800 a year before any town charge. That is a calculation from the posted rate, not a bill. The page also lists three town service districts that add to the town rate: Southridge at $0.03, Lafayette Ridge at $0.035 and Willow Shade at $0.02 (listed under 2025). The page notes that a public hearing on 2026 rates was scheduled for April 21, 2026 and adoption for May 5, 2026, so confirm the final figure with the office.

sections.h2: When are Culpeper County taxes due?
sections.html:
The county page says county taxes are due December 5 each year. That is one date, not the two installments used in neighboring counties.

The Treasurer takes payments by mail at Culpeper County Treasurer, PO Box 1447, Culpeper, VA 22701. The pages reviewed did not state the penalty or interest rate, so ask the Treasurer before a payment is late. If you sell in the fall, ask the closing agent to confirm what has been paid and how the December bill will be prorated.

sections.h2: How does Culpeper County reassess property?
sections.html:
Culpeper assesses every two years, on a biennial cycle set by the Board of Supervisors. The assessor's page says the current assessment became effective January 1, 2025 and stays in effect until January 1, 2027, with general reassessments falling in odd years.

The Department of Real Estate Assessments uses one or more of three methods:

  • Sales comparison: recent sales of similar properties, adjusted for size, condition, age, location and amenities.
  • Cost: current materials, labor and depreciation, plus the value of comparable vacant land.
  • Income: industry figures on what a property could earn and what it costs to run.

The same office runs the land use program, which must be revalidated at each general reassessment, and tax relief for elderly and disabled owners, disabled veterans and certain surviving spouses.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Culpeper County assessment?
sections.html:
The Board of Equalization is the formal route during a reassessment. It is an independent body appointed by the Circuit Court, and it can raise, lower or keep an assessment.

For the 2025 reassessment, the Board of Supervisors set May 1, 2025 for hearings to begin and June 20, 2025 as the last day to apply. The county page says the board is active during the period of the general reassessment, so ask the assessor for the dates tied to the next one.

After that, owners can apply to circuit court. Virginia Code 58.1-3984 lets an aggrieved taxpayer apply within the later of three years from the end of the tax year or one year from the assessment date, with the assessor's value presumed correct for real property.

sections.h2: What happens to Culpeper County tax and recording costs at closing?
sections.html:
Taxes on the house are a first lien. Virginia Code 58.1-3340 ranks the tax lien ahead of other liens until actual payment, requires sale proceeds to be applied to taxes and levies, and adds a lien on current-year rents.

The state grantor's tax on a deed is 50 cents per $500 of consideration under Virginia Code 58.1-802, and the seller pays it unless the buyer agrees to. The statute requires the clerk of the court where a deed is first recorded to certify that the tax was paid.

faqs.q: When are Culpeper County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: December 5 each year, according to the county's real estate tax page. Payments go to the Culpeper County Treasurer, PO Box 1447, Culpeper, VA 22701.

faqs.q: What is the Culpeper County tax rate for 2026?

faqs.a: Every two years. The current assessment took effect January 1, 2025 and remains until January 1, 2027.

faqs.a: June 20, 2025 was the final date to apply, with hearings starting May 1, 2025.
